patch.value: Fleet-amortized context assembly: attested, content-addressed shared assemblies plus a fleet-level token budget, so a thousand agents asking one question pay for one computation

Context cost is budgeted per invocation and paid per agent, so the same answer is recomputed and re-billed once for every agent that needs it. At fleet scale that is the dominant cost in the system and nothing in the design acknowledges it.

Measured on this workspace at 2,176 items on 2026.7.28, the loop AGENTS.md mandates costs roughly 6,100 tokens before an agent does any work:

  pm context --limit 10          7,075 B   about 1,770 tokens
  pm next                        8,603 B   about 2,150 tokens
  pm list-open --limit 20        4,713 B   about 1,180 tokens
  pm search <keywords> --limit 10  3,980 B   about   995 tokens

Those four answers are almost entirely a function of workspace state, not of who is asking. A thousand agents orienting on the same repository in the same minute compute the same ranking a thousand times and pay for it a thousand times, and the only thing that varies is the small part that is genuinely per-agent: the asker's claims, capabilities, and current focus. The economics invert as the fleet grows - the marginal agent adds almost no information to the assembly and pays full price for it.

The primitive that fixes this already has an owner and a name. pm-8bgeye makes an assembly record the inputs that produced it so the result can be reproduced and independently checked. An assembly that can state its inputs can be content-addressed by them, and a content-addressed assembly can be shared. This feature is the consumer of that attestation: a durable, addressable assembly cache plus a fleet-level budget, so the fleet pays once for the shared part and each agent pays only for its own delta.

Three things have to be true and none of them is true today.

First, the shared and the personal parts of an assembly must be separable, so the shared part can be addressed independently of the asker. Today they are computed together in one pass.

Second, the address must be honest. It must cover every input that can change the answer - the corpus version, the scoring configuration, the extension set, the budget, and the intent - or a stale assembly will be served as fresh. pm-77okxr is the cautionary precedent: folding one input into a cache identity while leaving the slot single made two legitimate invocation modes evict each other forever, at seven to twelve times the warm cost.

Third, the budget must exist at the fleet level. pm-5t33or declares per-command ceilings, which bound one answer. Nothing bounds the aggregate, so a fleet can be individually compliant and collectively ruinous, and no operator can see the total or set a target for it.

Boundaries. pm-4k6b entry (24) covers fleet-joint diversification, which deliberately makes different agents receive DIFFERENT context; this covers making identical requests share one computation, and the two must compose rather than conflict - diversification decides what each agent should see, amortization decides what a shared answer costs. pm-801d owns the derived read index that makes the underlying scan cheap; caching an assembly is a layer above it and neither substitutes for the other. pm-t5dt4z owns measuring cost per operation, which is the instrument this feature needs and not the mechanism.

A context assembly separates its state-derived part from its asker-derived part, and the state-derived part is addressed by a fingerprint over every input that can change it, enumerated in contract data rather than in code comments; Two agents issuing the same request against an unchanged workspace receive byte-identical shared assemblies and the second is served from the cache, proven by a test asserting one computation and two served results; The fingerprint is proven complete by a negative-control fixture per declared input: changing that input alone must change the address, so a stale assembly can never be served as fresh; The cache is a keyed store rather than a single slot, so distinct legitimate request shapes coexist instead of evicting each other, directly refuting the failure mode pm-77okxr records; A fleet-level token budget is declarable and observable: aggregate context spend across agents is reported over a window, and exceeding the target degrades deterministically by the same declared ladder a single command uses; Every served assembly carries its attestation, so a consumer can verify the shared part was produced by the inputs it claims without recomputing it; Amortization degenerates exactly to today's behaviour for a single agent on a small workspace, adding no cache lookup cost that a one-agent workspace can measure; Assemblies are invalidated by recorded workspace change rather than by wall-clock expiry, so correctness does not depend on a timeout

message: File fleet-amortized context assembly: the aggregate cost of orientation is unbudgeted and unshared
